harmonicFunction: A (I) - Crisp major tonic anchoring the brisk walking pace across Melbourne
E (V) - Dominant chord stepping down to D in the verse and propelling the chorus turnaround
D (IV) - Warm subdominant cushion in both the verse and chorus
Bm (ii) - Predominant minor second chord creating the pre-chorus lift
F#m (vi) - Relative minor chord opening the chorus with poignant nostalgia

techniques.name: Jangle-Rock Eighth-Note Strumming & Open Chords
techniques.description: Maintaining a propulsive 120 BPM acoustic rhythm with accented backbeats while weaving bright, open voicings and smooth transitions to Bm and F#m barre chords.

sequence: Drive the verse with crisp Down-Up eighth-note strumming across A, E, D, and A
Climb through the Bm → D → E pre-chorus with increasing dynamic intensity
Open up into full, ringing strums on the F#m → D → A → E chorus
Keep the right-hand wrist loose and bouncy at 120 BPM
tips: Keep your strumming motion compact and wrist-driven so the 120 BPM pace feels effortless and brisk
Let the open high E string ring during the A and E chords for extra jangle-pop shimmer
Practice transitioning smoothly into the Bm and F#m barre chords without breaking your right-hand strumming pulse
details.progression: A - E - D - A | F#m - D - A - E

techniques.name: Steve Connolly Chiming Upper-Triad Arpeggios & Telecaster Soloing
techniques.description: Steve Connolly's brilliant Australian jangle-guitar signature, using 9th-and-10th-fret upper triad inversions on strings 1, 2, and 3, coupled with ringing A major pentatonic melodic bends.

notes: 9th-position D-shape A major triad (9.3, 10.2, 9.1)
Step down to E major triad (9.3, 9.2, 7.1) and D major triad (7.3, 7.2, 5.1)
A major pentatonic target tones: A, B, C#, E, F#
Crisp Telecaster bridge pickup with light compressor sustain
sequence: Fret the 9th-fret D-shape A chord across strings 1, 2, and 3
Arpeggiate with clean alternate picking, allowing notes to ring into one another
Step down symmetrically to the E and D triad voicings
In the solo, add melodic bends on the high E string (fret 12 up to C#) before resolving smoothly
tips: Steve Connolly used a 1960s Fender Telecaster into a clean Fender Twin Reverb for bell-like clarity
Avoid resting your palm on the bridge—let all three triad strings chime continuously
Add a compressor pedal like an MXR Dyna Comp or Boss CS-3 to ensure every picked note rings at equal volume

sections.name: Intro Chiming Jangle Hook
sections.description: Steve Connolly's immortal opening jangle hook at the 9th fret over Paul Kelly's crisp acoustic rhythm strumming.
notes: Fret the D-shape A major triad at the 9th and 10th frets (9.3, 10.2, 9.1)
Let the notes ring together like a 12-string Rickenbacker or Telecaster
Step down cleanly through the E and D triad notes

sections.name: Verse 1 Melbourne Autumn Storytelling
sections.description: Brisk, walking-tempo A - E - D - A progression capturing the crisp autumn air of Melbourne ('I'm freezing my hands, I'm waiting on the corner...').
notes: Accent beats 2 and 4 with a crisp snare-like acoustic strum
Keep the E-to-D transition tight and clean
Maintain steady 120 BPM forward walking motion

sections.name: Pre-Chorus Dynamic Build ('Head Is Spinning')
sections.technique: Climbing ii - IV - V Barre Cadence
sections.description: The climbing ii - IV - V progression (Bm - D - E) building anticipation for the panoramic chorus release.
notes: Clean 2nd-fret barre on Bm
Increase strumming velocity into the E major chord
Prepare for the immediate drop into the F#m chorus downbeat

sections.name: Chorus Panoramic Anthem ('High on the Hill')
sections.description: Soaring F#m - D - A - E chorus looking out over Punt Road, Richmond, and the Melbourne Cricket Ground.
notes: Hit the 2nd-fret F#m barre chord firmly on beat 1 of the chorus
Let the D major and A major chords bloom with full sustain
Use the E major chord at the end of the line to launch into the next phrase

sections.name: Steve Connolly Guitar Solo & Jangle Break
sections.technique: A Major Pentatonic Lead & Triad Bends
sections.description: Steve Connolly's melodic Telecaster guitar solo weaving upper triads, singing A major pentatonic bends, and double stops over the A - E - D - A progression.
notes: Chiming Telecaster tone with light compression and subtle plate reverb
Whole-step bend on fret 12 of the high E string up to C#
Smooth descent resolving onto the root A triad at the 5th fret

sections.name: Outro MCG Climax & Chiming Fade
sections.description: The emotional finish where the band cycles through the chorus progression while Connolly's high 9th-fret arpeggios ring across the stereo field into the fade.
notes: Combine the F#m chorus rhythm with the high triad arpeggio hook
Maintain the buoyant 120 BPM tempo with no drag
Let the final chords ring out into natural studio decay

guitar.recommended: Takamine or Maton Dreadnought Acoustic (Paul Kelly) & Fender Telecaster (Steve Connolly)
guitar.pickup: Acoustic piezo/mic blend for rhythm; Telecaster bridge + neck pickup for jangle lead hooks

amp.recommended: Fender Twin Reverb or Vox AC30

effects.distortion: Clean boost or very light transparent overdrive for lead breaks
effects.other: Boss CS-3 Compression Sustainer for even, ringing jangle sustain

beginner.title: Open Verse Chords & Steady Pulse
steps: Master the open A, E, and D major chords
Practice the verse cycle (A - E - D - A) with steady eighth-note strumming at 100 BPM → 120 BPM
Use F#m7 (2-X-2-2-2-0) and Bm7 (X-2-0-2-3-2) as stepping stones for the barre chords

intermediate.title: Full Barre Chords & Pre-Chorus Lift
steps: Play the full Bm (2nd fret A-string barre) and F#m (2nd fret E-string barre) chords cleanly
Connect the Verse → Pre-Chorus (Bm - D - E) → Chorus (F#m - D - A - E) seamlessly
Lock in the brisk 120 BPM acoustic strumming groove

advanced.title: Steve Connolly's High Triad Hooks
steps: Learn the 9th-position triad arpeggio hook on the top three strings
Switch between rhythm strumming and the high electric hook for a two-guitar arrangement
Perform with full vocal storytelling and dynamic builds

commonMistakes: Slowing down when transitioning from open A or E into the Bm and F#m barre chords
Strumming too heavily with a stiff arm instead of keeping a light, brisk wrist motion
Choking the high E string during the 9th-fret triad arpeggio hook
practiceRoutine: 5 minutes: Verse A → E → D → A strumming warm-up at 120 BPM
5 minutes: Pre-chorus and chorus barre chord drill (Bm → D → E → F#m → D → A → E)
5 minutes: 9th-position triad arpeggio hook on strings 3, 2, and 1
focusAreas: Effortless 2nd-fret barre shifts between F#m and Bm
Clean note separation in the upper-register triad hook
metronomeWork: Start at 95 BPM to ensure the Bm and F#m barre changes land right on beat 1
Build to 120 BPM with crisp accents on beats 2 and 4
Practice the arpeggio hook against the metronome click without rushing
